notable_absence.finding: PREPARE, like the other read/write query statements in this batch, gates purely on the data-plane credential-type privilege pair (keyed to whatever statement is being prepared) and never on a management-plane capella-role:*. This is a genuine cross-product finding worth flagging distinctly: this is the first page in this round where the credential-type privilege explicitly varies *per prepared statement type* rather than being fixed for the page - the same PREPARE statement can require Read/Query Read (if preparing a SELECT) or Write+Read/Query Update+Query Read (if preparing an UPDATE). The privilege model composes with whatever DML the PREPARE wraps, rather than PREPARE having its own fixed privilege.

cross_component_finding: The Statement Cache section explicitly names both products in the same sentence - 'Prepared statements are stored in the prepared statement cache until you restart the Couchbase Server. In Couchbase Capella, the query engine uses the prepared statement cache to speed up the creation of prepared statements.' - and the Statement Propagation section does the same for query-node priming. No explicit 'Couchbase Server X.Y' version-gate citation is present on this page (so no recurrence of the known docs-issue is logged here), but the pattern of describing behavior in terms of 'restart the Couchbase Server' on a Capella page (where customers don't manage server restarts directly) is adjacent to that same issue family.
cross_product_finding: This page has explicit, textual, non-inferred links from SQL++'s PREPARE statement to the Java SDK's query-optimization guidance (concept-docs/n1ql-query.md#prepared-statements-for-query-optimization) and to SDK-side parameterized queries (howtos/sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md#parameterized-queries) - unlike the transaction-statement family in this same round, where the SQL++/SDK cross-reference was an open, unconfirmed question. Here the docs explicitly connect the SQL++ language feature to its SDK-side usage guidance, supporting a seeAlso relation with direct textual evidence.
